claims.text: Combining high heating rates, pre-imposed deformation, and subsequent annealing can induce a hierarchical microstructure in near-equiatomic HEAs.
The induced hierarchical microstructure consists of a disordered matrix containing uniformly distributed, coherent, high-modulus nanoprecipitates.
The proposed treatment will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young's modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally processed near-equiatomic HEAs often have single-phase or simple FCC/BCC multiphase microstructures.
Conventionally processed near-equiatomic HEAs exhibit tradeoffs among strength, ductility, stiffness, and fracture resistance.
Thermomechanical treatment can considerably improve the mechanical properties of a near-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA.
Nanoprecipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion and thereby increase yield and ultimate strength.
Load transfer through high-modulus nanoprecipitates increases the effective Young's modulus of the alloy.
Precipitate–matrix interfaces produce nanoscale crack bridging that enhances fracture resistance.
Nanoscale crack bridging can contribute to extrinsic fracture toughening in an HEA.
The nanoprecipitate-based strengthening and toughening mechanisms will maintain or improve ductility.
The proposed treatment can increase yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and Young's modulus by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional processing.
The proposed treatment will enhance ductility and fracture toughness through synergistic intrinsic and extrinsic toughening mechanisms.
The improvements should persist from ambient to moderately elevated temperatures and at strain rates typical of structural applications.
Excessively high temperatures, very high strain rates, or deleterious phase transformations can destabilize the engineered microstructure and eliminate its benefits.
Alloying-induced formation and growth of sigma phase can cause a noticeable loss of ductility in an HEA.
The quantitative property gains depend sensitively on alloy composition and processing parameters.
The long-term thermal and mechanical stability of the nanoprecipitate network remains unvalidated.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements of roughly 10–20% in strength, modulus, and fracture resistance without loss of ductility would falsify the hypothesis.
